name: Aarhus & Jutland
blurb: Denmark's second city, young and cheap by Danish standards, with a rainbow walkway on top of its art museum and Jutland's dunes, Viking mounds and moving sand to the north.
photoTopics: Aarhus Den Gamle By old town

name: Abel Tasman & Marlborough
blurb: New Zealand's sunniest corner — golden-sand coves you kayak between on the Abel Tasman track, and the Sauvignon Blanc vineyards of Marlborough.
photoTopics: Abel Tasman golden beach New Zealand

name: Abidjan & Grand-Bassam
blurb: West Africa's most cosmopolitan city — a lagoon skyline of glass towers, and down the coast a crumbling French colonial capital now a UNESCO site slowly being reclaimed by palm.

name: Abu Dhabi
blurb: Calmer and more considered than Dubai — the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, a Louvre outpost, and the Empty Quarter's dunes to the south.
photoTopics: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque Abu Dhabi
Qasr Al Watan palace Abu Dhabi

name: Acadia & the Maine Coast
blurb: Granite headlands, spruce and 45 miles of carriage roads built by a Rockefeller who hated cars. The first place in the United States to see the sunrise.

name: Accra & the Cape Coast
blurb: West Africa at its most welcoming: highlife bars, a serious art scene, and along the coast the slave forts of Elmina and Cape Coast, which are not an easy visit and should not be.

name: Adelaide & the Barossa
blurb: A planned colonial city ringed by parkland with world-class Shiraz an hour north, Kangaroo Island offshore, and a festival season that takes over the whole place in March.

name: Agadir & Taghazout
blurb: Atlantic point breaks, argan trees and 300 days of sun. A fishing village that became a surf town without entirely stopping being a fishing village.

name: Aitutaki
blurb: A lagoon repeatedly voted the most beautiful in the world, ringed by fifteen motu you can visit by day cruise, with a population small enough that everyone waves.

name: Alaska
blurb: Denali, tidewater glaciers calving into the sea, grizzlies catching salmon and the aurora from September. Vast, and only really open in summer.

name: Albanian Riviera
blurb: The Ionian coast Greece and Italy already sold: turquoise coves, Ottoman-era Gjirokastër inland, and Europe's last genuinely cheap beach.

name: Ålesund & Geirangerfjord
blurb: An Art Nouveau town rebuilt after burning down in 1904, at the mouth of the fjord country — Geiranger, Trollstigen's eleven hairpins, and Norway's most photographed cliff.

name: Almaty & the Tian Shan
blurb: A leafy Soviet-planned city with 4,000m peaks starting at the end of the tram line — you can ski at Shymbulak in the morning and be in a wine bar by six.

name: Alsace & Strasbourg
blurb: Half-timbered villages under vine-covered hills, a cathedral with an astronomical clock, and a cuisine that cannot decide whether it is French or German and is better for it.

name: AlUla
blurb: Nabataean tombs carved into sandstone cliffs, sister site to Petra and until very recently closed to almost everyone — Saudi Arabia's flagship reopening to tourism, and it shows.

name: Amalfi Coast
blurb: Pastel villages glued to vertical cliffs above impossibly blue water. Peerless in May and September; gridlocked and eye-watering in August.
photoTopics: Path of the Gods Amalfi hike

name: Amsterdam
blurb: Canal rings, Rembrandt and Van Gogh, and a bike-first city centre — beautiful, tolerant, and openly tired of stag parties.

name: Andorra
blurb: A 468-square-kilometre principality between France and Spain, run jointly by a bishop and the French president, with the biggest ski area in the Pyrenees and no VAT.

name: Angel Falls & Canaima
blurb: The tallest waterfall on earth, a kilometre of unbroken drop off a tabletop mountain older than the continents around it — reached only by small plane and dugout canoe.

name: Annecy & the Haute-Savoie
blurb: The cleanest lake in Europe, turquoise and ringed by Alps, with a canal-threaded old town on one shore and paragliders coming off the ridge above it all day.

name: Antalya & the Turquoise Coast
blurb: Roman ruins right on the beach, pine-covered mountains behind, and all-inclusive resorts at prices Western Europe cannot touch.

name: Antigua
blurb: 365 beaches — reputedly one for every day — plus Nelson's Dockyard, a working Georgian naval yard, and the Caribbean's best sailing week.

name: Antigua & Lake Atitlán
blurb: A pastel colonial town ringed by three volcanoes, with Lake Atitlán's Maya villages and the jungle temples of Tikal to the north.

name: Arequipa & Colca
blurb: A white volcanic-stone city under three volcanoes, with the deepest canyon in the world an hour north and condors riding the thermals out of it every morning.

name: Argentine Patagonia
blurb: The Perito Moreno glacier calving into a lake, and the granite spires of Fitz Roy above El Chaltén — Argentina's trekking capital.

name: Aruba
blurb: Outside the hurricane belt, so it delivers sun almost every day of the year — with a windswept desert interior and constant trade winds for kitesurfing.

name: Aspen & the Rockies
blurb: Four mountains, champagne powder and a former silver-mining town that became America's most glamorous ski resort. Superb hiking in summer too.

name: Asturias & the Green Coast
blurb: Cider poured from above the head, cliffs full of hidden beaches, and the Picos rising to 2,600 metres less than twenty miles from the sea. Nothing here looks like Spain.

name: Asunción & the Jesuit Missions
blurb: One of South America's oldest cities, laid-back and cheap, with the ruins of Jesuit reductions two hours south where Guaraní and Spanish priests built something briefly utopian.

name: Atacama Desert
blurb: The driest non-polar desert on earth — salt flats with flamingos, geysers at dawn at 4,300m, and skies so clear the world's biggest telescopes live here.
photoTopics: Valle de la Luna Atacama Chile

name: Athens
blurb: The Acropolis floating above a scruffy, energetic, brilliantly cheap city that has become one of Europe's best nights out.

name: Auckland & Bay of Islands
blurb: A city built on 48 volcanoes between two harbours, with black-sand surf beaches west, vineyards on Waiheke, and 144 subtropical islands north.

name: Austin & the Hill Country
blurb: Live music every night of the week, barbecue worth queuing four hours for, and swimming holes in the limestone hills west of town when the heat becomes unreasonable.
photoTopics: Austin Texas skyline Lady Bird Lake

name: Bagan
blurb: Over two thousand brick temples spread across a bend in the Irrawaddy, built in two hundred years and left standing for eight hundred more. Best seen from a bicycle at dawn.

name: Baku
blurb: A medieval walled old town beside three flame-shaped skyscrapers, oil wealth spent on architecture from Zaha Hadid, and mud volcanoes bubbling on the peninsula outside town.

name: Bali
blurb: Rice terraces, cliff temples, world-class surf and a wellness industry with its own gravity. Also, in the south, genuinely bad traffic.

name: Bandar Seri Begawan
blurb: A tiny oil-rich sultanate with a golden-domed mosque, the world's largest residential water village still lived in, and rainforest reserves right at the edge of town.
photoTopics: Ulu Temburong National Park canopy walk

name: Banff & Lake Louise
blurb: Glacier-fed lakes an unreal shade of turquoise beneath the Canadian Rockies, with the Icefields Parkway running north to Jasper.

name: Bangkok
blurb: Golden temples, canal markets and rooftop bars, wrapped around the best street food on earth. Relentless, humid and completely addictive.

name: Baños de Agua Santa
blurb: A small town wedged between an active volcano and a gorge, where hot springs, canyoning and a swing hung off a tree house at the edge of a cliff draw every adrenaline traveller in Ecuador.
tags: swing at the end of the world
photoTopics: Banos swing end of the world Ecuador

name: Barbados
blurb: Calm Caribbean beaches on the west, Atlantic surf on the east, rum distilleries in between, and a proper island culture beyond the resorts.

name: Barcelona
blurb: Gaudí's fever-dream architecture, a proper city beach and one of Europe's great eating and drinking cities — all walkable, all at once.

name: Bariloche & the Lake District
blurb: Alpine-style chocolate-shop town on a huge glacial lake, with South America's best skiing at Cerro Catedral and seven lakes to drive between.

name: Bath
blurb: Honey-coloured Georgian crescents around Roman baths, small enough to cover on foot and the Cotswolds ten minutes away.

name: Bavarian Alps
blurb: Neuschwanstein, painted villages and Germany's highest peak — gentler and cheaper skiing than the big Alpine names.

name: Beijing
blurb: The Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven and the best-preserved stretches of the Great Wall — imperial China at full scale.

name: Belfast & the Causeway Coast
blurb: A city that has changed beyond recognition in thirty years, with the Titanic story told properly and, an hour north, forty thousand basalt columns going into the sea.

name: Belgrade
blurb: A city destroyed and rebuilt forty-odd times, sitting where two big rivers meet, with floating river clubs, a fortress park and a nightlife that genuinely does not stop.

name: Belize
blurb: The Great Blue Hole and the Caribbean's longest barrier reef, Maya temples in the jungle, and everyone speaks English.

name: Berat & Gjirokastër
blurb: Two Ottoman towns of stacked stone houses — Berat's thousand windows climbing the hillside, Gjirokastër's slate roofs — both still lived in rather than curated.

name: Bergen & the Fjords
blurb: A wooden Hanseatic wharf, seven mountains and the gateway to the Sognefjord and Nærøyfjord. Also, famously, the rain capital of Europe.

name: Berlin
blurb: Europe's most restless capital: brutal 20th-century history, the best club scene in the world, and still cheap for a major city.

name: Bhutan
blurb: The last Himalayan kingdom, deliberately limiting tourism with a daily fee — fortress monasteries, archery and Gross National Happiness.

name: Biarritz & the French Basque Country
blurb: Where European surfing began, in a town Napoleon III built for an empress, with Basque villages of red-and-white timber a few miles inland and pintxos across the border.

name: Big Sur & the Central Coast
blurb: Ninety miles of Highway 1 clinging to cliffs above the Pacific, redwoods running down to the sea, and a bridge that has appeared in more car adverts than any road in the world.

name: Bilbao & the Basque Coast
blurb: A steel town that bet everything on a titanium art museum and won, with pintxos bars in the old quarter and a coast of surf beaches and a hermitage on a rock.

name: Birmingham
blurb: England's self-declared second city — more miles of canal than Venice, a jewellery quarter that still makes most of the UK's rings, and one of the country's best curry scenes concentrated along the Balti Triangle.

name: Black Forest
blurb: Dense fir forest, cuckoo clocks, thermal spa towns and a surprising density of Michelin stars along a famous scenic drive.

name: Bodrum
blurb: Turkey's smartest resort town — a Crusader castle, whitewashed streets, gulet cruises and a nightlife scene that runs till dawn.

name: Bogotá
blurb: Eight million people at 2,600 metres, with a colonial old town, the best gold museum on earth, and a Sunday when 120km of road closes to cars entirely.

name: Bohol & Cebu
blurb: The Chocolate Hills and the world's smallest primate, plus canyoneering to Kawasan Falls and thresher sharks off Malapascua.

name: Bologna & Emilia-Romagna
blurb: Forty kilometres of arcades, the oldest university in Europe, and the region that gave the world Parmigiano, prosciutto di Parma, balsamic and tagliatelle al ragù.

name: Bora Bora & Tahiti
blurb: The lagoon that invented the overwater bungalow — a volcanic peak ringed by a turquoise reef, with Mo'orea and the Tuamotus nearby.

name: Boracay
blurb: White Beach is four kilometres of powder-fine sand and legendary sunsets — closed and cleaned up in 2018, and much better for it.

name: Bordeaux
blurb: A honey-stone 18th-century city that cleaned itself up beautifully, surrounded by the most famous vineyards on earth.
photoTopics: Place de la Bourse water mirror Bordeaux

name: Borneo (Sabah)
blurb: Orangutans and proboscis monkeys on the Kinabatangan river, Southeast Asia's highest peak, and Sipadan — one of the world's great dive sites.

name: Bornholm
blurb: A granite island closer to Sweden than Denmark, with four round fortress churches, smokehouses with white chimneys, and Northern Europe's best beach on its southern tip.

name: Boston
blurb: America's most walkable and most European city — revolutionary history on the Freedom Trail, Harvard across the river, and New England autumn.
photoTopics: Boston Freedom Trail Old State House

name: Bratislava
blurb: A compact, walkable capital on the Danube close enough to Vienna for a day trip, with a hilltop castle, a quirky UFO-topped bridge, and prices a fraction of its Austrian neighbour.

name: Brighton
blurb: London-by-the-sea: a Regency seafront, an Indian-palace pavilion built by a prince with more money than taste, and the least buttoned-up city in England.

name: Brisbane & the Sunshine Coast
blurb: A subtropical river city that finally grew into itself, with Moreton Bay's sand islands on one side and the Glass House Mountains an hour north.

name: Bristol
blurb: A harbour city that funded itself on the slave trade and has spent recent decades reckoning with it — now Banksy's home town, with balloons over Brunel's bridge every August.

name: Brittany
blurb: Celtic France: granite ports, megalithic stones, tidal islands and crêperies — cooler and wilder than the south, and far cheaper.

name: Brno & Moravia
blurb: Czechia's second city, with a functionalist villa that changed architecture, a genuinely strange cathedral bell habit, and the country's wine region rolling away to the south.

name: Broome & the Kimberley
blurb: Red pindan cliffs meeting turquoise water at Cable Beach, and behind it one of the last true wildernesses — gorges, 40,000-year-old rock art, and roads that close for half the year.

name: Bruges
blurb: A perfectly preserved medieval merchant town of canals, belfries and Flemish primitives — plus the best beer and chocolate in Europe.

name: Brussels
blurb: The EU's capital, but also a city of comic-strip murals, gilded guildhalls on the Grand Place, and more chocolatiers per square mile than seems entirely necessary.

name: Bucharest
blurb: Belle Époque villas next to the second-largest building on earth, a nightlife the rest of Europe hasn't caught up with, and prices that make it feel like a mistake.

name: Budapest
blurb: Grand Habsburg boulevards, thermal baths built like palaces, and ruin bars in derelict courtyards — outstanding value for a capital.

name: Buenos Aires
blurb: Paris with steak and tango — grand boulevards, the world's most beautiful bookshop, milongas until dawn and Malbec at every table.

name: Burgundy
blurb: The most obsessively subdivided vineyards on earth, where a single road separates wines that cost £30 and £3,000, plus Romanesque abbeys and Beaune's tiled hospice roof.

name: Bwindi & the Ugandan Rift
blurb: Mountain gorillas in a forest that has been standing for 25,000 years, plus chimpanzees at Kibale and tree-climbing lions in Queen Elizabeth. Green, steep and very wet.

name: Byron Bay
blurb: Australia's easternmost point — long surf beaches, a lighthouse walk with whales offshore, and a wellness-and-markets culture that defines the place.

name: Cafayate & the Calchaquí Valleys
blurb: The world's highest-altitude wine region, red rock canyons carved into shapes with names like the amphitheatre and the devil's throat, and torrontés grown nowhere else quite like this.

name: Cairo & Giza
blurb: The last surviving wonder of the ancient world on the edge of a city of 20 million — plus the Grand Egyptian Museum and Islamic Cairo.

name: Cape Town
blurb: Table Mountain rising straight out of a city between two oceans, with world-class wine half an hour away. Spectacular, and unequal.

name: Cape Verde
blurb: Ten Atlantic volcanic islands with year-round warmth six hours from Europe — Sal's windsurfing, Santo Antão's hiking, and morna music everywhere.
photoTopics: Pico do Fogo volcano Cape Verde

name: Cappadocia
blurb: Volcanic 'fairy chimneys', rock-cut churches and underground cities — and a dawn sky filled with a hundred balloons.
photoTopics: Goreme Open Air Museum rock church

name: Cardiff
blurb: Wales' compact capital, a Norman castle sitting in the middle of the shopping streets, a redeveloped bay full of restaurants where the docks used to be, and rugby internationals that shake the city on match day.

name: Cartagena
blurb: A walled Spanish colonial port of bougainvillea and balconies on the Caribbean, with the Rosario Islands an hour offshore.

name: Cebu & Bohol
blurb: Whale sharks off Oslob, tarsiers the size of a fist in Bohol's forests, and the Chocolate Hills — over a thousand identical mounds turning brown every dry season.

name: Český Krumlov
blurb: A tiny medieval town looped by a river beneath an enormous castle — a day trip from Prague that deserves an overnight.

name: Chamonix
blurb: Under the summit of Mont Blanc: serious off-piste in winter, serious alpinism in summer, and a town that never pretends otherwise.

name: Chapada Diamantina
blurb: A plateau of table mountains, underground rivers you can swim through by torchlight, and a waterfall that free-falls so far the water turns to mist before it lands.
photoTopics: Morro do Pai Inacio Chapada Diamantina

name: Charleston
blurb: Pastel antebellum houses, cobbled streets and live oaks dripping Spanish moss — plus one of the best restaurant scenes in the country.

name: Chefchaouen
blurb: A mountain town painted every shade of blue, small enough to walk in an afternoon and pleasant enough that most people stay three days longer than planned.

name: Chengdu
blurb: Giant pandas, teahouses in the park and the most gloriously numbing food in China — the gateway to Tibet and the Sichuan mountains.

name: Chiang Mai
blurb: A moated old city of 300 temples in the northern hills — cooking schools, ethical elephant sanctuaries and the world's biggest digital-nomad scene. Avoid March–April burning season.
photoTopics: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep Chiang Mai
Yi Peng lantern festival Chiang Mai

name: Chiapas & Palenque
blurb: Maya temples rising out of jungle canopy, a canyon a thousand metres deep with crocodiles at the bottom, and San Cristóbal's highland markets in cloud most mornings.
photoTopics: San Cristobal de las Casas Mexico

name: Chicago
blurb: The birthplace of the skyscraper, with a lakefront beach and cycle path, world-class museums and blues bars. Winters are genuinely brutal.

name: Chiloé
blurb: Wooden churches built without a single nail, stilt houses in fishing coves, and folklore about a ghost ship that still shapes how people talk about the sea.

name: Churchill
blurb: The polar bear capital of the world, reachable only by train or plane, where beluga whales fill the river in summer and the aurora runs most clear nights in winter.

name: Cinque Terre
blurb: Five stacked fishing villages on a vertiginous coast, linked by cliff paths and a train — tiny, gorgeous, and utterly swamped in summer.

name: Cluj-Napoca & Timișoara
blurb: Romania's student capital and its most European city — a huge tech scene, one of the biggest music festivals on the continent, and Timișoara's Habsburg squares to the west.

name: Cologne & the Rhine
blurb: A cathedral that took 632 years and is worth every one of them, a beer served in small glasses by waiters who keep bringing more, and castles up the river all the way to Mainz.

name: Côn Đảo
blurb: A former prison island now half national park, with empty beaches, nesting turtles and a colonial cemetery that Vietnamese visitors come to at midnight.

name: Cook Islands
blurb: Rarotonga's mountainous interior ringed by a lagoon, and Aitutaki's — arguably the most beautiful lagoon on earth. No building taller than a palm tree.

name: Copenhagen
blurb: The design and food capital of the North: bikes everywhere, harbour swimming in the middle of the city, and Noma's long shadow.

name: Copper Canyon
blurb: A canyon system four times the size of the Grand Canyon, crossed by a railway engineers said could not be built, through Tarahumara country where people still run a hundred miles for fun.

name: Córdoba
blurb: The Mezquita — a forest of eight hundred candy-striped arches with a cathedral dropped into the middle — plus flower-filled patios and the hottest summers in Europe.

name: Corfu
blurb: The greenest Greek island, with Venetian and British architecture in the old town and olive groves running down to sheltered bays.

name: Cork & West Cork
blurb: Ireland's food capital, built on islands in a river, with the English Market at its centre and a coastline west of it of coves, islands and very good seafood.

name: Cornwall
blurb: Britain's surf coast: turquoise coves, fishing harbours, coast path walking and a food scene well above its weight.

name: Corsica
blurb: 'The mountain in the sea': granite peaks, the brutal GR20 trek and some of the Mediterranean's most beautiful and least built-up beaches.

name: Costa Rica
blurb: Five percent of the planet's biodiversity in a country the size of Wales — volcanoes, cloud forest, two coastlines and no army since 1948.
photoTopics: Red eyed tree frog Costa Rica

name: Crete
blurb: Greece's biggest island is really a small country: Minoan palaces, a 16km gorge, mountain villages and beaches you can still have to yourself.

name: Curaçao
blurb: Dutch-Caribbean pastel waterfronts in Willemstad, hidden coves under limestone cliffs, and shore diving straight off the beach. Outside the hurricane belt.

name: Cusco & Machu Picchu
blurb: The Inca capital at 3,400m — colonial churches built on Inca foundations, the Sacred Valley, and the four-day trail to Machu Picchu.

name: Cyprus
blurb: The Med's warmest, longest season — swim into November — with Byzantine mountain churches and Roman mosaics inland.

name: Dahab & Sinai
blurb: A Bedouin town on the Gulf of Aqaba where the reef starts a few metres offshore and the Blue Hole draws divers who really ought to know better.

name: Dakar & Gorée
blurb: Africa's westernmost city — mbalax blasting from every taxi, surf on both sides of the peninsula, and Gorée Island twenty minutes offshore.

name: Delhi & Agra
blurb: Mughal tombs, Old Delhi's chaos and the Taj Mahal two hours away. Overwhelming, extraordinary, and unbearable in May and June.

name: Denver & the Front Range
blurb: A mile-high city with 300 days of sun and the Rockies an hour west — Red Rocks for concerts, fourteeners for weekends, and more breweries than anywhere in America.

name: Dhaka & Old Dhaka
blurb: One of the densest cities on earth, with a river of ten thousand wooden boats, Mughal forts sinking gently into the silt, and a rickshaw art tradition recognised by UNESCO.

name: Diani & the Kenyan Coast
blurb: White sand and Indian Ocean reef on the Swahili coast, with Mombasa's old town and colobus monkeys in the coastal forest.

name: Doha
blurb: A serious museum city behind the skyline — the Museum of Islamic Art, a rebuilt souq, and the inland sea where dunes meet the Gulf.
photoTopics: Khor Al Adaid inland sea Qatar

name: Dominica
blurb: The Nature Island — nine active volcanoes, 365 rivers, a boiling lake you hike five hours to reach, and almost no beaches, which is why the cruise crowds go elsewhere.

name: Donegal
blurb: Ireland's forgotten corner: Slieve League's cliffs are three times the height of the Cliffs of Moher, and almost nobody is standing on them.

name: Dresden & Saxon Switzerland
blurb: A baroque capital burned to the ground in 1945 and rebuilt stone by numbered stone, with sandstone towers and a bridge across a gorge in the national park east of it.

name: Dubai
blurb: Superlatives made concrete — the tallest building, enormous malls, brunch culture and desert dunes half an hour out. Unliveable heat from June to September.

name: Dublin
blurb: Georgian squares, extraordinary literary history and the best pub culture anywhere — compact, sociable and eye-wateringly expensive.

name: Dubrovnik
blurb: A perfectly preserved walled city rising out of the Adriatic. Walk the walls at dawn, before the cruise ships and the heat arrive.
photoTopics: Mount Srd cable car Dubrovnik view

name: Durmitor & the Tara Canyon
blurb: Forty-eight peaks over two thousand metres, eighteen glacial lakes, and the deepest river canyon in Europe running 1,300 metres down through the middle of it.

name: Easter Island
blurb: The most remote inhabited island on earth — 3,700km from anywhere — and 900 moai staring inland from the world's most enigmatic archaeological site.

name: Edinburgh
blurb: A volcanic crag with a castle on it, a medieval Old Town, a Georgian New Town — and in August, the biggest arts festival in the world.

name: El Nido & Palawan
blurb: Limestone islands in impossibly clear lagoons, reached by bangka boat — plus an underground river and the wreck diving of Coron.
photoTopics: Bacuit Bay island hopping El Nido

name: El Salvador's Surf Coast
blurb: Central America's most consistent point breaks, volcanoes you can climb before breakfast, and pupusas griddled fresh on every corner — still years behind Costa Rica on price.
photoTopics: El Tunco surf beach El Salvador

name: Esperance & the South Coast
blurb: The whitest sand in Australia, kangaroos that actually sleep on the beach, and a national park coastline so far from anywhere it barely makes the tourist maps.

name: Essaouira
blurb: A blue-and-white Atlantic port with ramparts, gnaoua music and relentless wind — Morocco's kitesurfing capital and its most relaxed medina.

name: Eswatini's Reserves
blurb: Africa's last absolute monarchy, small enough to cross by car in a morning, with rhino you can walk beside on foot and a reed dance ceremony held every year for the king.

name: Ethiopia
blurb: Rock-hewn churches at Lalibela, castles at Gondar and the Simien Mountains — never colonised, with its own calendar, script and coffee ceremony.

name: Everest Region
blurb: Two weeks on foot through Sherpa villages and monasteries to the foot of the highest mountain on earth. Not a holiday — an expedition.

name: Faroe Islands
blurb: Eighteen green, sheer-sided islands in the North Atlantic — grass-roofed villages, sea stacks and a waterfall that falls into the ocean.

name: Fès
blurb: The largest car-free urban area on earth — a 1,200-year-old medina of 9,000 alleys, tanneries and the world's oldest university.

name: Fiji
blurb: 333 islands, soft-coral diving that divers travel the world for, and a welcome — *bula* — that is genuinely not a marketing slogan.

name: Finnish Lapland
blurb: Snowy forest, glass igloos, huskies and the official Santa Claus Village — which is why December here is the busiest month of the year.

name: Fiordland & Milford Sound
blurb: Mitre Peak rising 1,700m straight out of the water, waterfalls everywhere after rain — and it rains 200 days a year, which is when it's best.
photoTopics: Milford Sound Mitre Peak New Zealand

name: Fish River Canyon
blurb: The second-largest canyon on earth, 160km long and 550m deep, crossed by a five-day hike with no facilities at all — a hot spring at the far end is the only reward.

name: Florence
blurb: The Renaissance in one walkable square mile — and the gateway to Tuscany's vineyards and hill towns when the queues get too much.

name: Florianópolis
blurb: Forty-two beaches on one island — surf on the east, calm bays on the west, sand dunes and lagoons, and Brazil's best quality of life.

name: Galápagos Islands
blurb: The islands that gave us evolution — and the only place on earth where the wildlife has no fear of you. Sea lions, marine iguanas, giant tortoises.

name: Galicia & Santiago
blurb: Green, Celtic and wet — the end of the Camino, drowned river valleys full of shellfish, Albariño from vines trained overhead, and the wildest coast in Spain.

name: Galle & the South Coast
blurb: A Dutch-walled fort town, surf breaks at Weligama, blue whales off Mirissa and stilt fishermen at sunset.

name: Galway & Connemara
blurb: A small, riotously musical city on the Atlantic, with the bogs and mountains of Connemara and the Cliffs of Moher on the doorstep.

name: Garden Route
blurb: A 300km coastal drive of forest, lagoons and empty beaches, with bungee jumps, whale watching at Hermanus and elephant sanctuaries.

name: Gdańsk
blurb: A rebuilt Hanseatic merchant city on the Baltic — amber, extraordinary WWII and Solidarity museums, and beaches on the tram line.

name: Geneva
blurb: A lakeside city of diplomats and watchmakers, with a 140-metre fountain marking the water's edge, Mont Blanc visible on a clear day, and enough international organisations to fill a small country.

name: George Town, Penang
blurb: George Town's UNESCO shophouses and street art wrapped around Asia's best hawker food — arguably the single greatest eating city in the region.
photoTopics: Penang hawker food char kway teow

name: Ghent & Antwerp
blurb: Bruges without the coach parties: Ghent has the guild houses and a huge student population, Antwerp has Rubens, diamonds and the best fashion school in Europe.

name: Glacier & Waterton Lakes
blurb: A hundred jagged peaks straddling the US-Canada border on the Going-to-the-Sun Road, with grizzlies, mountain goats, and glaciers that are visibly disappearing.
photoTopics: Going to the Sun Road Glacier

name: Glasgow
blurb: Edinburgh's rougher, funnier, friendlier neighbour — Mackintosh architecture, free world-class museums, and a live music scene per head that beats almost anywhere.

name: Goa
blurb: Portuguese churches and palm-backed beaches — party-heavy in the north, genuinely sleepy in the south. Dead from June to September.

name: Gold Coast
blurb: Seventy kilometres of surf beach beneath a high-rise skyline, Australia's biggest theme parks, and subtropical rainforest twenty minutes inland.

name: Golden Bay & Farewell Spit
blurb: Golden sand coves at the top of the South Island, and beyond them a sand spit running thirty kilometres into the Tasman Sea, home to one of the largest gannet colonies on earth.

name: Gorongosa
blurb: A park nearly wiped out by civil war and rebuilt from a few hundred surviving animals to one of Africa's great conservation comebacks — lions, elephants and a rainforest-topped mountain.

name: Gothenburg & the West Coast
blurb: Sweden's second city — canals, a serious seafood habit, and just north of it the Bohuslän archipelago, eight thousand granite islands scoured smooth by ice.

name: Gotland & Visby
blurb: A Hanseatic walled town of merchant warehouses and ruined churches on a limestone island, with sea stacks along the shore and more sunshine than anywhere else in Sweden.

name: Gozo & Comino
blurb: Malta's slower sister — a citadel on a hill, terraced fields, salt pans cut into the rock, and between the two islands a lagoon of implausible blue.

name: Gran Canaria
blurb: A 'continent in miniature' — dunes at one end, pine forest and ravines in the middle, and Europe's most established gay resort scene at Maspalomas.

name: Granada
blurb: The Alhambra above, free tapas below, and the Sierra Nevada close enough to ski in the morning and sit in the sun by lunch.
photoTopics: Alhambra Granada from Mirador San Nicolas

name: Granada & Ometepe
blurb: A candy-coloured colonial city on a freshwater sea, with an island of two volcanoes in the middle of it and Pacific surf ninety minutes west. Central America at half the price.
photoTopics: San Juan del Sur surf Nicaragua

name: Grand Canyon
blurb: 446km long, 1.6km deep and genuinely impossible to photograph adequately. Rim-to-rim hikes, mule trains and rafting the Colorado below.

name: Graz & Styria
blurb: Austria's second city, with a Renaissance old town, a bright blue blob of a modern art museum dropped next to it, and the pumpkin-seed-oil country rolling south.

name: Great Barrier Reef & Cairns
blurb: The largest living structure on earth, and the only place where two World Heritage sites meet — the reef and the Daintree rainforest.
photoTopics: Great Barrier Reef aerial Heart Reef
Green sea turtle Great Barrier Reef

name: Grenada
blurb: The Spice Isle — nutmeg and cocoa plantations, rainforest waterfalls, an underwater sculpture park, and far fewer visitors than its neighbours.

name: Guadalajara & Tequila
blurb: The birthplace of mariachi and tequila both, with a walkable colonial centre, a huge student population, and the actual town of Tequila an hour away for distillery tours.

name: Guernsey, Sark & Herm
blurb: Quieter than Jersey, with Victor Hugo's exiled house in St Peter Port and Sark next door — no cars at all, and the first Dark Sky island in the world.

name: Guilin & Yangshuo
blurb: The karst peaks from every Chinese scroll painting, rising out of the Li River — best seen from a bamboo raft or a bike in the paddy fields.

name: Ha Long Bay
blurb: Nearly 2,000 limestone islands rising from jade water, seen from an overnight junk. Go to quieter Lan Ha Bay if you can.
photoTopics: Junk boat Ha Long Bay Vietnam

name: Hakone & Mount Fuji
blurb: Volcanic hot-spring country in the shadow of Fuji — open-air onsen, a lake with a pirate ship, and outstanding modern art museums.
photoTopics: Mount Fuji from Lake Ashi Hakone

name: Hallstatt & the Salzkammergut
blurb: The most photographed village in Austria, wedged between a mirror lake and a cliff, in a region of 76 lakes and salt mines.

name: Hamburg
blurb: More bridges than Venice and Amsterdam combined, a spectacular concert hall, red-brick warehouses and a famously rowdy harbour quarter.

name: Hampi
blurb: The ruins of a city that once held half a million people, scattered across 40 square kilometres of surreal granite boulders. Bouldering, temples and coracle rides.

name: Hanoi
blurb: A thousand-year-old capital of lakes, French villas and a motorbike-choked Old Quarter where the best food comes off a plastic stool.
photoTopics: Hoan Kiem Lake Ngoc Son temple

name: Havana & Cuba
blurb: Crumbling Baroque grandeur, 1950s American cars, live son in every doorway and tobacco fields in Viñales. Nowhere else feels like this.

name: Hawaii — Big Island
blurb: Active lava at Kīlauea, black and green sand beaches, and the world's best observatory site on Mauna Kea — where it also snows.

name: Hawke's Bay & Napier
blurb: A town flattened by an earthquake in 1931 and rebuilt entirely in Art Deco, surrounded by New Zealand's oldest vineyards and the sunniest weather in the country.

name: Heidelberg & the Rhine-Neckar
blurb: Germany's oldest university under a ruined red castle on a wooded hill, with a philosophers' walk on the far bank and the Neckar valley opening east.

name: Heligoland
blurb: A red sandstone rock 50km out in the North Sea — British until 1890, bombed almost out of existence, now duty-free, car-free, and covered in gannets each spring.

name: Helsinki
blurb: Understated, design-obsessed and built on a sea of islands — with the world's best public saunas and a ferry to Tallinn.

name: Hiroshima & Miyajima
blurb: A moving Peace Memorial and a rebuilt, warm-hearted city — with the floating torii gate of Miyajima a short ferry away.

name: Ho Chi Minh City
blurb: Vietnam's engine room — French colonial boulevards, sobering war history, rooftop bars and a street-food culture that never sleeps.
photoTopics: Ho Chi Minh City skyline Saigon river
War Remnants Museum Ho Chi Minh City

name: Hội An
blurb: A perfectly preserved trading port of tailors, lantern-lit lanes and riverside cafés, with a good beach and My Son's Cham ruins nearby.
photoTopics: Hoi An old town yellow walls
Thu Bon river boats Hoi An

name: Hokkaido & Furano
blurb: Lavender fields and rolling farmland in July, three metres of the lightest snow on earth by January, and crab, uni and dairy that the rest of Japan queues for.

name: Hong Kong
blurb: The world's most dramatic harbour skyline, with hiking trails and empty beaches twenty minutes from the trading floor.
photoTopics: Hong Kong street market Mong Kok
Dragon's Back hiking trail Hong Kong

name: Hpa-An
blurb: Limestone karst towers standing straight out of green paddy, riddled with caves full of Buddhas and a lot of bats. Climb Mount Zwegabin at dawn and sleep at the monastery.
photoTopics: Kyauk Ka Lat pagoda rock Myanmar

name: Huaraz & the Cordillera Blanca
blurb: The highest tropical mountain range on earth: sixteen peaks over 6,000m, glacial lakes the colour of antifreeze, and the Santa Cruz trek to walk between them.

name: Hvar
blurb: Lavender fields and hidden pebble coves by day, superyachts and famously messy bars by night — Croatia's most glamorous island.

name: Hydra & the Saronic Gulf
blurb: An island where cars are banned outright — donkeys carry the luggage, sea captains' mansions climb the amphitheatre of the harbour, and Athens is ninety minutes away.

name: Ibiza
blurb: The world's loudest island for four months of the year — and a quiet, pine-scented, startlingly beautiful one for the other eight.
photoTopics: Ibiza sunset Cafe del Mar San Antonio

name: Iceland & the South Coast
blurb: Glaciers, black beaches, geysers and waterfalls within a day's drive of the capital — plus the aurora from September to March.

name: Iguazú Falls
blurb: 275 waterfalls across nearly 3km of jungle on the Brazil–Argentina border. The Devil's Throat is one of the loudest places on earth.

name: Iguazú from the Argentine Side
blurb: Two hundred and seventy-five separate falls in a horseshoe of jungle, with walkways that put you close enough to the Devil's Throat to feel the spray from a kilometre away.

name: Ikaria & Samos
blurb: Ikaria is one of the world's Blue Zones, where people forget to die and nobody keeps to a timetable. Samos next door grows the sweet muscat wine and has Pythagoras' birthplace.

name: Inle Lake
blurb: A shallow highland lake where fishermen row standing on one leg, whole villages sit on stilts, and tomatoes are grown on floating gardens of woven weed.

name: Interlaken & the Jungfrau
blurb: Between two lakes below the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau — Europe's adventure-sport capital and the highest railway station on the continent.

name: Isle of Skye
blurb: Jagged Cuillin ridges, sea cliffs and rock formations with names out of folklore. Beautiful, busy in summer, and very wet.
photoTopics: Old Man of Storr Isle of Skye

name: Istanbul
blurb: The only city on two continents: Byzantine and Ottoman monuments, a vast bazaar, and ferries criss-crossing the Bosphorus at dusk.

name: Istria
blurb: Croatia's Tuscany: hilltop towns, truffles, olive oil and Venetian harbours, with none of the Dalmatian crush.

name: Jaffna & the North
blurb: Tamil Sri Lanka, closed to visitors for thirty years and only now reachable: palmyra palms, an enormous Hindu temple complex, and a causeway to islands with wild ponies.

name: Jaipur & Rajasthan
blurb: The Pink City of hill forts, stepwells and palace hotels — the most photogenic corner of India, and the gateway to the Thar desert.

name: Jaisalmer & the Thar Desert
blurb: A sandcastle-coloured fort still lived in by five thousand people, with camel safaris into dunes at the edge of the Thar Desert and a border with Pakistan close enough to see the wire.

name: Jamaica
blurb: The birthplace of reggae — Blue Mountain coffee, jerk pits, waterfalls you can climb and the Seven Mile Beach at Negril.

name: Jeju Island
blurb: A volcanic island of lava tubes, waterfalls and Korea's highest peak, walked end to end on the 400km Olle coastal trail.

name: Jericoacoara
blurb: Sand streets, no traffic lights, a dune you climb every evening to watch the sunset with everyone else in town, and consistent kitesurfing wind almost year-round.

name: Jersey
blurb: Nine miles by five, closer to France than England and belonging to neither — a tidal range of twelve metres that doubles the island twice a day, and German tunnels underneath it.
photoTopics: Jersey beach low tide Channel Islands

name: Jerusalem
blurb: Four quarters, three faiths and three thousand years inside one square kilometre of walls. Nowhere else is as densely layered.

name: Jiuzhaigou & Sichuan
blurb: A valley of turquoise terraced lakes so vivid they look photoshopped, in a province that also gives you giant pandas, the numbingly spicy hotpot, and Tibetan monasteries in the western hills.

name: Kaieteur Falls
blurb: Five times the height of Niagara and four times the width, in rainforest so untouched you can fly there for the day and see almost nobody else at all.
photoTopics: Cock of the rock Guyana bird

name: Kaikōura & the Coromandel
blurb: A submarine canyon a kilometre offshore brings sperm whales, dusky dolphins and albatross within sight of snow-capped mountains. Crayfish straight off the boat.

name: Kampot & Kep
blurb: Riverside French shophouses going gently to seed, the pepper that French chefs still specify by name, and an abandoned hill station in the clouds above.

name: Kanazawa & the Noto Coast
blurb: The Kyoto that the war never touched: intact samurai and geisha districts, one of Japan's three great gardens, and gold leaf on everything including the ice cream.

name: Kandy & the Hill Country
blurb: Tea estates, waterfalls and the Nine Arch Bridge, linked by what may be the most beautiful train ride in the world.
photoTopics: Nine Arch Bridge Ella Sri Lanka
Sri Lanka tea plantation Nuwara Eliya

name: Kangaroo Island
blurb: A third the size of Wales with a third of its wildlife density — sea lions hauled out on the sand, koalas in every second tree, and remarkable granite boulders worn round by wind.

name: Karlovy Vary & Bohemian Switzerland
blurb: A spa town of pastel colonnades where you sip hot mineral water from a special spouted cup, and to the north sandstone arches and gorges out of a Romantic painting.

name: Kars & Ani
blurb: A Russian-built town on a freezing high plateau, and forty minutes away the ghost city of Ani — a medieval Armenian capital of a hundred thousand people, alone on the border.

name: Kathmandu Valley
blurb: Seven UNESCO sites in one valley — pagoda-roofed durbar squares, the great stupa of Boudhanath, and the staging post for every Himalayan trek.

name: Kauai
blurb: The oldest and greenest Hawaiian island — the Nā Pali cliffs, Waimea Canyon and a helicopter ride you will not forget. Very wet, very beautiful.

name: Kaunas
blurb: Lithuania's interwar 'temporary capital', with the largest collection of Art Deco and Bauhaus architecture in Central Europe and a hilltop confluence of two rivers that locals picnic beside all summer.

name: Kefalonia & Zakynthos
blurb: Green Ionian islands with cypress on limestone: Myrtos beach a thousand feet below the road, Melissani's underground lake, and a shipwreck on sand the colour of icing sugar.

name: Kerala
blurb: Backwater houseboats, tea plantations in the Western Ghats, Ayurveda and Kathakali — India at its greenest and most relaxed.

name: Kerry & Dingle
blurb: Ireland's most dramatic corner: the Ring of Kerry, the Dingle peninsula, Atlantic cliffs and trad music in tiny harbour pubs.

name: Kilimanjaro
blurb: The highest free-standing mountain in the world, and the only 5,895m summit an unroped walker can reach — through five climate zones in six days.

name: Koh Lanta
blurb: The antidote to Phuket: long quiet west-facing beaches, sunset bars with no bass, and easy diving on Hin Daeng. Half of it shuts in low season.
photoTopics: Mu Ko Lanta national park lighthouse

name: Koh Samui
blurb: Coconut-palm island on the Gulf side, so it stays dry when the Andaman coast is drowning — and it's the ferry hop to the Full Moon Party.

name: Komodo & Flores
blurb: Dragons on one island, pink sand on the next, and some of the richest reef diving anywhere — reached by liveaboard from Labuan Bajo.

name: Kotor & the Bay
blurb: A fjord-like bay ringed by mountains, with a walled medieval town and a fortress staircase that earns you the view.
photoTopics: Perast and Our Lady of the Rocks

name: Krabi & Railay
blurb: Vertical limestone karsts straight out of the Andaman Sea — world-class rock climbing on Railay, and beaches only reachable by longtail.

name: Kraków
blurb: Poland's beautiful old capital — Europe's largest medieval market square, the Jewish quarter of Kazimierz, and Auschwitz an hour away.
photoTopics: Krakow Main Market Square Cloth Hall

name: Kruger & the Lowveld
blurb: The most accessible Big Five safari on earth — you can self-drive it — plus the Blyde River Canyon on the escarpment above.

name: Kuala Lumpur
blurb: Malay, Chinese and Indian food within one block, colonial arcades under the Petronas Towers, and rainforest inside the city limits.
photoTopics: KL Forest Eco Park canopy walk

name: Kyoto
blurb: Two thousand temples, geisha districts and raked gravel gardens. Transcendent in November; shoulder-to-shoulder during cherry blossom.

name: Kyushu & Beppu
blurb: Japan's volcanic south: 2,000 hot springs in one town, an active caldera you can drive into at Aso, and the best tonkotsu ramen anywhere, which is where it was invented.

name: La Paz & the Sea of Cortez
blurb: Cousteau's "aquarium of the world": whale sharks in the bay from October, sea lions at Espíritu Santo, and grey whales calving on the Pacific side every winter.

name: La Paz & the Yungas
blurb: A city poured into a canyon at 3,600 metres, with cable cars for public transport and a road down to the jungle that used to kill 300 people a year.
photoTopics: La Paz Bolivia cable car city

name: Ladakh
blurb: A high-altitude cold desert of Tibetan monasteries and 5,000m passes between the Karakoram and Himalaya. Only reachable from May to October.

name: Lagos
blurb: Africa's biggest city and the beating heart of Nollywood and Afrobeats — a lagoon metropolis of twenty million people, buzzing art scenes and beach clubs on Victoria Island.

name: Lahore
blurb: Mughal Pakistan's cultural capital — a fort and mosque built by emperors, a food street that stays loud until 3am, and a border ceremony at dusk with more theatrical marching than seems strictly necessary.

name: Lake Balaton
blurb: Central Europe's largest lake and Hungary's summer playground — shallow, warm, and lined with beach towns, with the volcanic Tihany peninsula and its lavender fields splitting the shoreline in two.

name: Lake Bled & the Julian Alps
blurb: A church on an island in an emerald lake below a cliff-top castle, with Triglav National Park and the Soča valley behind it.

name: Lake Como
blurb: Villas, gardens and steep wooded mountains dropping straight into deep blue water — the most theatrical of the Italian lakes.

name: Lake District
blurb: England's mountains and lakes in a compact, walkable national park — with proper pubs, and rain you should simply plan for.

name: Lake Malawi
blurb: The third-largest lake in Africa, warm as bathwater, with more species of fish than any other lake on earth and beaches nobody flies eleven hours to compete for.

name: Lake Ohrid
blurb: One of the oldest and deepest lakes in Europe, with a town of 365 churches on the shore, Byzantine frescoes, and water clear enough to see thirty metres down.

name: Lamu
blurb: A Swahili town of coral-stone houses and carved doors where there are no cars, only donkeys and dhows, and very little has changed since the fourteenth century.
photoTopics: Lamu old town Kenya carved door

name: Langkawi
blurb: A duty-free archipelago of mangrove geoparks and rainforest-backed beaches, with a sky bridge slung between two peaks.

name: Lanzarote
blurb: A lunar volcanic island where an artist wrote the building code — no high-rises, no billboards, black lava vineyards and startling light.

name: Las Vegas
blurb: A neon fever dream in the Mojave — residencies, buffets, pool parties and casinos, with Red Rock and the Grand Canyon on the doorstep.

name: Leipzig
blurb: Where Bach worked for 27 years and where the Monday demonstrations brought the GDR down — now a city of converted cotton mills, cheap studios and very good coffee.

name: Lençóis Maranhenses
blurb: 1,500 square kilometres of white dunes that fill with rainwater every July, becoming a desert full of turquoise freshwater lagoons you can swim across.

name: Liechtenstein
blurb: A principality of 40,000 people between Switzerland and Austria, ruled from a castle above the capital, with a 75km trail from end to end and a ski village at the top.

name: Lima
blurb: One of the world's great food cities — ceviche, Nikkei and several of the world's top 50 restaurants — on cliffs above the Pacific.

name: Lisbon
blurb: Seven hills, yellow trams, tiled façades and fado in the back streets — with Atlantic surf beaches half an hour down the line.

name: Liverpool
blurb: A great Victorian port that got very rich, then very poor, and is now neither — with more listed buildings than anywhere outside London and a sense of humour about all of it.

name: Liwonde & the Nyika Plateau
blurb: A small park along the Shire River packed with elephants and reintroduced rhino, and far to the north a rolling highland plateau that looks more like Scotland than Africa.

name: Ljubljana & Piran
blurb: A capital small enough to cross on foot, remodelled by one architect with a dragon fixation, and forty kilometres of Adriatic coast ending in a Venetian town on a spit.

name: Lofoten Islands
blurb: Granite peaks rising straight from the Arctic sea above red fishermen's cabins — midnight sun in June, aurora from September.

name: Lombok & the Gilis
blurb: Bali twenty years ago: an active volcano to trek, empty south-coast surf beaches, and three car-free islands with turtles offshore.

name: London
blurb: Free world-class museums, the best theatre on earth and a genuinely global food scene — priced like the world capital it is.

name: Los Angeles
blurb: Beaches, canyons, studios and the best Mexican and Korean food outside their home countries — spread over 80km, so hire a car.

name: Los Cabos & Baja
blurb: Desert meeting the Sea of Cortez — Jacques Cousteau's 'aquarium of the world' — with grey whales calving in winter and world-class sportfishing.

name: Los Roques
blurb: A national park of forty-two cays and a lagoon so pale turquoise it barely looks real, once ranked among the best beaches in the world and reachable only by small plane.

name: Luang Prabang
blurb: A UNESCO town of gilded temples and French shophouses between two rivers — dawn alms-giving, turquoise waterfalls, and a very slow pulse.

name: Lucerne
blurb: A covered wooden bridge, a painted old town and a lake ringed by mountains you can ride cogwheel trains up. Switzerland's greatest hits.

name: Luxembourg
blurb: A fortress city on two gorges, tunnelled through with 17km of casemates, with free public transport across the whole country and Moselle vineyards down the eastern border.

name: Luxor & Aswan
blurb: The greatest open-air museum on earth — Karnak, the Valley of the Kings and Abu Simbel — best seen from a slow boat down the Nile.

name: Lyon
blurb: France's gastronomic capital, with Renaissance secret passageways, two rivers and the Alps ninety minutes away.
photoTopics: Basilica Notre Dame de Fourviere Lyon

name: Madagascar
blurb: An island that split off 88 million years ago — 90% of its wildlife exists nowhere else. Lemurs, baobabs and spiny forest. Infrastructure is hard.

name: Madeira
blurb: A vertical Atlantic garden island — levada walks through laurel forest, sheer sea cliffs and mild weather every single month.

name: Madrid
blurb: Spain's confident, unhurried capital: the world's best art triangle, tapas until 2am, and no coastline to distract you.

name: Mafia Island
blurb: Zanzibar's quiet neighbour — a marine park with whale sharks feeding close to shore from October, and almost no development at all beyond a handful of small lodges.

name: Mallorca
blurb: Far more than the package-holiday cliché: a serious mountain range, hidden coves, world-class road cycling and a genuinely good capital.

name: Malta
blurb: 7,000 years of history on a limestone rock — megalithic temples, a Baroque capital and world-class diving, all in English.

name: Manaus & the Amazon
blurb: A rubber-boom opera house in the middle of the largest rainforest on earth, and downriver the meeting of the waters where two rivers run side by side for miles without mixing.

name: Manchester
blurb: The first industrial city in the world, now living off music, football and red brick. Two of the biggest clubs on earth, the Northern Quarter, and an unrepentant amount of rain.

name: Marbella & Costa del Sol
blurb: Golf, yachts and 320 days of sun, with the white villages and the Sierra de las Nieves twenty minutes inland when you want out.
photoTopics: Marbella old town Plaza de los Naranjos

name: Marrakech
blurb: A walled medina of souks, riads and snake charmers under the Atlas Mountains. Sensory overload, and three hours from most of Europe.

name: Marseille & the Calanques
blurb: France's oldest and least polite city — a Greek port that became Algerian, Italian and Comorian all at once — with white limestone fjords starting where the suburbs stop.
photoTopics: Notre Dame de la Garde Marseille

name: Martinique & Guadeloupe
blurb: France in the Caribbean: rum distilleries with appellation rules, patisseries in the tropics, black-sand beaches under a volcano, and rainforest in the middle of it all.

name: Masai Mara
blurb: The Great Migration crossing the Mara River between July and October — nearly two million wildebeest, and the crocodiles waiting for them.
photoTopics: Hot air balloon safari Masai Mara

name: Matera & Basilicata
blurb: Cave dwellings carved into a ravine and lived in continuously for nine thousand years — cleared as a national disgrace in the 1950s, now a European Capital of Culture.

name: Maui
blurb: The Road to Hana, sunrise above the clouds on Haleakalā, humpback whales in winter and some of the best snorkelling in the Pacific.

name: Mauritius
blurb: Lagoons inside a near-continuous reef, sugarcane and volcanic peaks inland, and a Creole-Indian-Chinese-French food culture all its own.

name: Medellín
blurb: The City of Eternal Spring — 22°C every day of the year, cable cars up the hillsides, a remarkable turnaround story, and coffee country next door.

name: Meghalaya
blurb: The wettest place on earth, where the Khasi grow bridges out of living fig roots over rivers so clear the boats look like they are floating in air.

name: Melbourne
blurb: Laneway coffee and street art, the best sport calendar in the world, and the Great Ocean Road three hours west. Four seasons in one day, reliably.

name: Mendoza
blurb: Malbec country in the rain shadow of Aconcagua — vineyards with 6,000m peaks behind them, long lunches, and rafting in the Andes.

name: Menorca
blurb: The quiet Balearic — a biosphere reserve with no high-rises, a bridle path running the whole way round the island, and coves you can only reach on foot.

name: Mérida & the Yucatán
blurb: A safe, elegant colonial city of pastel mansions, with cenotes, flamingos and the great Maya cities of Uxmal and Chichén Itzá around it.

name: Meteora
blurb: Six working monasteries balanced on sandstone pillars up to 400 metres high, reached for centuries only by rope ladder and net. Now there are steps, which helps.

name: Mexico City
blurb: Aztec ruins under colonial palaces, Frida Kahlo's house, the world's best street food and a spring-like climate all year at 2,240m.
photoTopics: Palacio de Bellas Artes Mexico City

name: Miami
blurb: Art Deco on South Beach, a Cuban-American culture that runs the city, and the Everglades and Keys within a couple of hours.

name: Milan
blurb: Italy's business and fashion capital: less obviously pretty than its rivals, but unbeatable for design, aperitivo and opera.

name: Milos
blurb: A volcanic island with more than seventy beaches, no two alike — Sarakiniko's white lunar rock, Kleftiko's sea caves, and fishing villages with garage doors painted in every colour.

name: Monaco & the Riviera
blurb: Two square kilometres of superyachts, a casino you must dress for, and a Grand Prix run through streets that are otherwise a rather formal seaside town.

name: Mongolia
blurb: The emptiest country on earth — Gobi dunes, endless steppe, nomad ger camps and eagle hunters. Brutally cold outside a short summer.

name: Montréal
blurb: French North America — cobbled Vieux-Montréal, an extraordinary festival calendar, bagels and smoked meat, and a mountain in the middle.

name: Moorea
blurb: Bora Bora's less famous sister — jagged volcanic peaks over a lagoon of the same impossible turquoise, at a fraction of the price and twenty minutes by ferry from Tahiti.

name: Mozambique's Coast
blurb: A thousand miles of Indian Ocean that most people fly over. Dhows, whale sharks off Tofo, and the Bazaruto archipelago's sandbars turning turquoise at low tide.

name: Munich
blurb: Beer halls, superb galleries and river surfing in a park bigger than Central Park — with the Alps an hour south.

name: Muscat & Oman
blurb: The Gulf without the glass towers — whitewashed forts, wadis you can swim in, turtle beaches and the Empty Quarter. Genuinely welcoming.

name: Mykonos
blurb: Whitewashed cubist alleys by day, one of the Mediterranean's most glamorous and expensive party scenes by night.

name: Namibia
blurb: The world's oldest desert meeting the Atlantic — 300m rust-red dunes at Sossusvlei, the Skeleton Coast, and Etosha's waterholes.

name: Napa & Sonoma
blurb: The wine region that beat France in 1976 — hot-air balloons over the vines at dawn, three-star restaurants, and redwoods over the ridge.

name: Naples
blurb: Chaotic, operatic and gloriously unpolished — the best pizza on earth, Pompeii and Vesuvius on the doorstep, and prices half of Rome's.
photoTopics: Naples Gulf view Castel dell Ovo

name: Nashville
blurb: Live music in every bar on Broadway from 10am, the Grand Ole Opry, hot chicken, and the Smoky Mountains three hours east.

name: Naxos
blurb: The Cyclades without the price tag: enormous sandy beaches, a mountainous interior of marble villages, and a working island economy.

name: New Caledonia
blurb: The world's largest lagoon, enclosed by a 1,500km barrier reef, with French bakeries on one side and Kanak villages on the other.
photoTopics: Isle of Pines New Caledonia beach
Heart of Voh mangrove New Caledonia

name: New Orleans
blurb: Jazz born here, Creole and Cajun cooking, wrought-iron balconies in the French Quarter, and a Mardi Gras that swallows the city whole.
photoTopics: Jazz band Frenchmen Street New Orleans

name: New York City
blurb: Still the densest concentration of things to do on earth — museums, Broadway, food from everywhere, and a park the size of a town in the middle.
photoTopics: Metropolitan Museum of Art New York

name: Newfoundland
blurb: Icebergs drifting past fishing outports, whales in the bays, Gros Morne's fjords and the only confirmed Viking site in North America.

name: Ngapali Beach
blurb: Three miles of white sand and fishing boats on the Bay of Bengal, with no high-rises and, for most of the year, almost nobody on it.

name: Nice & the Côte d'Azur
blurb: A long pebble bay under palm trees, an Italianate old town, and Monaco, Antibes and Saint-Tropez strung along the coast beside it.
photoTopics: Nice old town Cours Saleya market

name: Ningaloo & Exmouth
blurb: A 260km fringing reef you can wade to from the beach, with whale sharks from March and humpbacks after that. The Great Barrier Reef without the crowds or the boats.

name: Niseko
blurb: The deepest, driest, most reliable powder on the planet — 15 metres a season — with onsen at the bottom of the run.

name: Normandy
blurb: Mont-Saint-Michel cut off by the tide, the D-Day beaches, Bayeux's embroidered account of 1066, and cream, cider and Camembert in between.

name: Northumberland & Hadrian's Wall
blurb: The edge of the Roman empire, running 73 miles coast to coast, with the darkest skies in England above it and castles on empty beaches to the east.

name: Nova Scotia & Cape Breton
blurb: The Cabot Trail winding along cliffs above the Atlantic, fishing villages painted in primary colours, Gaelic still spoken in places, and the world's highest tides next door.
photoTopics: Cabot Trail Cape Breton Nova Scotia
Bay of Fundy tides Nova Scotia

name: Novi Sad
blurb: Serbia's laid-back second city, its Habsburg-era fortress overlooking the Danube hosting one of Europe's biggest summer music festivals, EXIT, in what used to be an ammunition store.

name: Oaxaca
blurb: Mexico's culinary and craft capital — seven moles, mezcal palenques, Zapotec ruins at Monte Albán and the most intense Day of the Dead anywhere.
photoTopics: Day of the Dead Oaxaca altar

name: Okavango Delta
blurb: A river that never reaches the sea, flooding into the Kalahari and drawing enormous game — explored by mokoro canoe through the reeds.

name: Okinawa
blurb: Subtropical Japan — coral reefs, its own distinct Ryukyu culture and cuisine, and one of the longest-lived populations on earth.

name: Olympic National Park
blurb: Rainforest, glaciated mountains and a wild Pacific coast in a single park — moss-draped Hoh Rainforest gets twelve feet of rain a year, and the coastline nearby gets none of the crowds.

name: Osaka
blurb: Japan's kitchen — louder, cheaper and far more up-for-it than Tokyo, with Kyoto and Nara twenty minutes away.

name: Oslo
blurb: A capital wedged between a fjord and a forest, with superb modern museums and cross-country ski trails inside the city limits.

name: Otavalo & the Ecuadorian Highlands
blurb: The largest indigenous market in the Americas, held every Saturday beneath a ring of volcanoes, with weavers still using techniques unchanged since before the Inca arrived.

name: Oxford & Cambridge
blurb: Eight hundred years of college quadrangles, punts on the river, libraries you need permission to enter, and an intense unspoken rivalry that surfaces once a year on the Thames.

name: Palau
blurb: Jellyfish Lake, where millions of stingless jellyfish drift and you can swim among them; below the water, a wall dive so famous it's on every diver's list before they've dived anywhere else.

name: Palm Springs & Joshua Tree
blurb: Mid-century modern houses under a 3,000m mountain, pools everywhere, and an hour east a national park of granite piles and trees that look drawn by Seuss.
photoTopics: Palm Springs mid century modern house

name: Panama
blurb: Ships climbing the canal beside a glass skyline and a UNESCO old town — with the San Blas islands and Bocas del Toro on two different oceans.

name: Paraty & the Costa Verde
blurb: A Portuguese gold-rush port of white houses and cobbles so uneven they were designed to flood at spring tide, with 65 islands and 300 beaches offshore.

name: Paris
blurb: Still the benchmark: the Louvre, the boulevards, the bistros and the bakeries — best in the shoulder seasons when the queues thin out.

name: Paros & Antiparos
blurb: The Cyclades done properly: a marble island with a Byzantine capital, the best windsurfing in Greece, and a village of white lanes that looks like everyone's idea of Greece.

name: Pembrokeshire
blurb: Britain's only coastal national park: 186 miles of clifftop path, puffins on Skomer, and beaches that on the four good days a year could pass for the Caribbean.

name: Perth & Margaret River
blurb: The world's most isolated major city — endless white beaches, quokkas on Rottnest, and the Margaret River wine and surf region three hours south.

name: Peruvian Amazon
blurb: Riverboat and lodge country upstream of Iquitos — pink river dolphins, canopy walkways and the densest birdlife on the planet.

name: Petra & Wadi Rum
blurb: A Nabataean city carved into rose sandstone, reached through a slot canyon — then Mars-red desert where you sleep in a Bedouin camp under the stars.
photoTopics: Bedouin camp Wadi Rum night sky

name: Phuket
blurb: Thailand's biggest island: everything from Patong's full-volume strip to quiet northern bays, and the launch point for Phang Nga Bay.
photoTopics: Phang Nga Bay James Bond island

name: Picos de Europa
blurb: Green, wet, wildly under-visited limestone mountains twenty miles from the sea — cider, blue cheese and some of Spain's best walking.
photoTopics: Picos de Europa Naranjo de Bulnes
Cares Gorge trail Picos de Europa

name: Plitvice & Krka
blurb: Sixteen terraced lakes falling into one another over travertine barriers that are still growing, connected by miles of boardwalk laid inches above turquoise water.

name: Plovdiv & the Rhodopes
blurb: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in Europe, with a Roman theatre still used for opera, a hill of painted merchant houses, and the Rhodope mountains behind.

name: Pokhara & Annapurna
blurb: A lakeside town with 8,000m peaks reflected in the water, and the trailhead for the Annapurna Circuit and Poon Hill.

name: Portland
blurb: Food carts on every block, more breweries per head than anywhere in America, and the only city with a bookstore big enough to need a map. An hour from mountains and coast both.

name: Porto
blurb: Granite, port wine and azulejo tiles stacked above the Douro — smaller and grittier than Lisbon, and many people's favourite for it.
photoTopics: Port wine cellars Vila Nova de Gaia

name: Poznań
blurb: Where Poland began — a cathedral island holding the tombs of the first kings, a Renaissance town hall where two mechanical goats butt heads at noon, and croissants worth a detour.
photoTopics: Poznan old market square town hall

name: Prague
blurb: A gothic and baroque city that came through the war intact — spires, a castle, the world's cheapest great beer, and enormous crowds.
photoTopics: Prague old town square astronomical clock

name: Prince Edward Island
blurb: Red sandstone cliffs, potato fields, and the fictional home of Anne of Green Gables — Canada's smallest province, and possibly its friendliest.
photoTopics: Anne of Green Gables house PEI

name: Provence
blurb: Lavender rows, hilltop villages, Roman aqueducts and rosé — with the mistral wind and, in July, an awful lot of company.

name: Pucón & the Chilean Lakes
blurb: A perfect cone of a volcano you can climb in a day and ski down in winter, ringed by lakes, hot springs and the last of the monkey-puzzle forests.

name: Puerto Rico
blurb: Old San Juan's blue cobblestones and fortresses, the only tropical rainforest in the US park system, and three bioluminescent bays.
photoTopics: Old San Juan colourful street Puerto Rico

name: Puerto Vallarta
blurb: Cobbled old town and a long malecón on Banderas Bay, jungle-backed beaches reachable only by boat, and Mexico's most welcoming LGBTQ+ scene.

name: Puglia
blurb: Italy's heel: whitewashed hill towns, conical trulli houses, olive groves to the horizon and two coastlines with barely a high-rise.

name: Punta Cana
blurb: Fifty kilometres of palm-lined white sand and the Caribbean's densest concentration of all-inclusive resorts. Reliable, easy and good value.

name: Québec City
blurb: The only walled city north of Mexico — a 400-year-old French fortress town that becomes a genuine fairy tale under snow.
photoTopics: Quebec City old town winter snow

name: Queenstown
blurb: The self-declared adventure capital of the world — bungee was invented here — on a lake beneath the Remarkables, with four ski fields in winter.

name: Quito & the Andes
blurb: The best-preserved colonial centre in the Americas at 2,850m, ringed by volcanoes — Cotopaxi, Quilotoa's crater lake and the equator itself.

name: Raja Ampat
blurb: The most biodiverse marine environment on the planet — 1,500 islands, 75% of all known coral species, and almost nobody there. Hard to reach, worth it.

name: Rangiroa & the Tuamotus
blurb: One of the largest atolls on earth, a coral ring so big the lagoon has its own horizon — dive the pass at the right tide and hundreds of grey sharks stream past in the current.

name: Rarotonga
blurb: A single extinct volcano ringed by reef, small enough to cycle round in an afternoon, with a Saturday market and a night-market food scene that punches well above its size.

name: Réunion
blurb: A French département in the Indian Ocean built around an active volcano and three collapsed craters. The best hiking island in the world, and it is not close.
photoTopics: Piton de la Fournaise Réunion volcano

name: Rhodes
blurb: A complete medieval walled city you can sleep inside, plus a long sunny season and beaches on both a calm and a windy coast.
photoTopics: Palace of the Grand Master Rhodes

name: Riga
blurb: The largest collection of Art Nouveau architecture in Europe, a huge covered market in old Zeppelin hangars, and Baltic prices.
photoTopics: Riga Art Nouveau facade Alberta iela
Riga old town House of Blackheads

name: Rio de Janeiro
blurb: Christ the Redeemer over Sugarloaf, Copacabana and Ipanema, and a Carnival that stops the country. The setting is genuinely without equal.
photoTopics: Christ the Redeemer Rio de Janeiro

name: Rishikesh
blurb: The yoga capital of the world on the Ganges where it leaves the Himalaya — ashrams, white-water rafting and no alcohol anywhere.

name: Roatán & the Bay Islands
blurb: The southern end of the second-largest barrier reef on earth, and the cheapest place in the world to learn to dive. Whale sharks off Utila, and English still spoken from the buccaneer days.

name: Rome
blurb: Three thousand years of ruins, basilicas and Baroque fountains stacked on top of each other, with the food to match. Relentless in August.

name: Ronda & the White Towns
blurb: A town split by a 120-metre gorge with a bridge across it, and a scattering of whitewashed villages through the hills behind — one of them painted entirely blue.
photoTopics: Setenil de las Bodegas rock houses

name: Rotorua & Taupō
blurb: Geysers, bubbling mud and the smell of sulphur, with the strongest living Māori culture in the country and the Tongariro Crossing to the south.

name: Rotterdam & Utrecht
blurb: Rotterdam was flattened in 1940 and rebuilt as an architectural experiment; Utrecht kept its medieval centre and put cafés on the wharves below street level.

name: Rügen & the Baltic Coast
blurb: Chalk cliffs above beech forest that Caspar David Friedrich painted, sixty kilometres of white sand, and resort towns of white filigree villas from the 1880s.

name: Rwanda
blurb: Mountain gorilla trekking in the Virunga volcanoes — an hour on foot to sit with a habituated family. Also the cleanest country in Africa.

name: Sa Pa
blurb: Terraced rice valleys in the far north, trekked between homestays in Hmong and Dao villages, under Vietnam's highest peak.

name: Saaremaa & Hiiumaa
blurb: Estonia's islands kept their own dialect and windmills through fifty years as a closed Soviet border zone, which is precisely why they still feel untouched.

name: Sahara & the Atlas
blurb: Camel out over the Erg Chebbi dunes to a desert camp, then drive back through Berber villages and the kasbahs of the High Atlas.

name: Saint Lucia
blurb: The Pitons rising straight out of the sea, a drive-in volcano, rainforest and some of the Caribbean's most romantic hotels.
photoTopics: Sulphur Springs drive-in volcano St Lucia

name: Salar de Uyuni
blurb: The world's largest salt flat — 10,000km² of blinding white that becomes a perfect mirror of the sky when it floods between January and March.

name: Salta & the Northwest
blurb: Argentina's high desert: seven-coloured mountains at Purmamarca, salt flats at 3,400m, and the world's highest-altitude Malbec grown at Cafayate.
photoTopics: Purmamarca hill of seven colours Argentina

name: Salvador da Bahia
blurb: The heart of Afro-Brazilian culture — Pelourinho's baroque colour, capoeira in the squares, candomblé, and the best street carnival in Brazil.

name: Salzburg
blurb: Mozart's baroque hometown under a hilltop fortress, with the Sound of Music lakes and the Alps starting at the edge of town.

name: Samarkand & Bukhara
blurb: The Silk Road's showpiece — cobalt-tiled madrasas, Timur's tomb and Registan square, plus Bukhara's intact medieval centre.

name: Samoa
blurb: The heart of Polynesia, where fa'a Samoa still runs daily life, you sleep in an open beach fale for twenty pounds, and the To Sua ocean trench is exactly as good as the photographs.

name: San Antonio
blurb: The Alamo, a Riverwalk of restaurants below street level, and the most Mexican city in the US that isn't in Mexico — five Spanish missions still standing from the 1700s.

name: San Diego
blurb: The most consistently pleasant weather in the US, 70 miles of beach, the best zoo in America and a serious craft beer scene.
photoTopics: La Jolla Cove San Diego seals

name: San Francisco
blurb: Fog, hills and the Golden Gate, with Alcatraz in the bay and the redwoods and Napa within two hours. Summer is the coldest season here.
photoTopics: Golden Gate Bridge San Francisco fog

name: San Marino
blurb: The world's oldest surviving republic, founded in 301 AD, sitting on a limestone crag with three towers along the ridge and a view to the Adriatic on a clear day.

name: San Pedro de Atacama
blurb: The driest non-polar desert on earth, ringed by 6,000m volcanoes, with geysers steaming at dawn, salt flats full of flamingos, and clearer skies than almost anywhere for astronomy.
photoTopics: Valle de la Luna Atacama Chile

name: San Sebastián
blurb: A perfect shell-shaped bay, more Michelin stars per head than almost anywhere, and pintxos bars you could happily never leave.
photoTopics: San Sebastian old town Parte Vieja

name: Sani Pass & the Maloti
blurb: An entire country above 1,000m, reachable by a switchback pass so steep only 4x4s attempt it, with Africa's highest pub at the top and pony trekking to villages with no roads at all.

name: Santa Fe & Taos
blurb: Adobe architecture protected by law, the oldest capital city in the US, a genuinely serious art market, and green chile on absolutely everything.

name: Santiago
blurb: A modern capital hemmed in by the snow-capped Andes — ski in the morning, Pacific coast at Valparaíso in the afternoon, wine valleys in between.

name: Santorini
blurb: A drowned volcanic caldera ringed with white-and-blue villages. The most photographed sunset in Europe, and priced accordingly.

name: Sarajevo & Mostar
blurb: A city where a mosque, a synagogue, an Orthodox and a Catholic church stand within a few hundred metres, still marked by the longest siege in modern history — and Mostar's bridge, rebuilt.

name: Sardinia
blurb: Caribbean-grade water on a Mediterranean island, with a fiercely distinct interior of Bronze Age towers, shepherds and mountains.

name: Savannah & the Lowcountry
blurb: Twenty-two garden squares under live oaks dripping with Spanish moss, antebellum houses, and a drinking law that lets you carry your glass down the street.

name: Scottish Highlands
blurb: Empty glens, sea lochs and Britain's biggest mountains — spectacular, moody, and in June you should genuinely worry about the midges.

name: Seattle
blurb: Coffee, grunge and Pike Place, ringed by water and volcanoes — Rainier, the Olympics and the North Cascades all within reach. It really does rain.

name: Sedona
blurb: Red rock buttes glowing at sunset, said by some to sit on energy vortexes, with world-class mountain biking and Slide Rock's natural water chute for when it gets hot.

name: Seoul
blurb: Palaces beside skyscrapers, mountains inside the city, 24-hour everything and the fastest internet on the planet.

name: Serengeti & Ngorongoro
blurb: Endless plains and the Ngorongoro Crater — a collapsed caldera holding 25,000 animals inside its walls. The classic African safari.

name: Seville
blurb: Moorish palaces, orange trees and flamenco in the courtyards — spectacular in spring, genuinely dangerous in an August heatwave.

name: Seychelles
blurb: Granite boulders on pink-white sand at Anse Source d'Argent — probably the most photographed beach on earth — and giant tortoises on Aldabra.
photoTopics: Vallee de Mai coco de mer

name: Shanghai
blurb: Art-deco riverfront facing a skyline from a science-fiction film, with the best cocktail bars and modern galleries in China.

name: Sharm el-Sheikh & the Red Sea
blurb: Some of the best and cheapest reef diving anywhere — Ras Mohammed and the Blue Hole — with guaranteed sun and all-inclusive resorts.
photoTopics: Red Sea coral reef diving Egypt

name: Siargao
blurb: The Philippines' surf capital — Cloud 9's reef break, coconut palms to the horizon, rock pools and a very good time.

name: Sicily
blurb: Greek temples, Arab-Norman churches, Europe's most active volcano and arguably Italy's best food — on an island big enough to need two weeks.

name: Siem Reap & Angkor
blurb: The largest religious monument on earth, plus a thousand more temples swallowed by jungle — and a town that has learned how to feed and water you.

name: Siena & the Val d'Orcia
blurb: A medieval city that runs a bareback horse race round its shell-shaped square twice a year, set in the cypress-and-hilltop landscape everyone pictures when they think of Tuscany.

name: Sifnos & Folegandros
blurb: Two islands the crowds have not found: Sifnos is where Greeks go to eat, and Folegandros has a cliff-top village 200 metres straight above the sea with no airport at all.

name: Similan Islands & Khao Lak
blurb: Nine granite islands in the Andaman Sea repeatedly ranked among the best dive sites on earth, closed half the year to let the reef recover — Thailand's most protected stretch of coast.

name: Singapore
blurb: A city-state that works flawlessly: hawker centres with Michelin stars, supertrees, and the tidiest, safest introduction to Asia there is.
photoTopics: Gardens by the Bay Supertrees Singapore

name: Sintra & the Serra
blurb: A cool green hill where Portuguese royalty and rich romantics competed to build the most ludicrous palace, plus Europe's westernmost cliffs and Atlantic surf beaches below.

name: Skardu & the Karakoram
blurb: Base camp country for K2 and the Karakoram's giants, with cold desert dunes improbably stacked beside glacial lakes and expeditions setting off every summer for the world's hardest mountain.

name: Snowdonia & North Wales
blurb: Slate, sheep and serious mountains — the training ground for Everest, the fastest zip line in the world, and castles Edward I built to make a point.

name: Sofia & the Rila Mountains
blurb: A capital with a 2,290m mountain inside the city limits, Roman ruins under the metro stations, and the Rila Monastery's striped arcades an hour and a half south.

name: Song-Köl & the Tien Shan
blurb: An alpine lake at 3,000m surrounded by summer pasture, where families still move up with their herds in June and you sleep in a yurt with no road worth the name to get there.

name: South Luangwa
blurb: The birthplace of the walking safari, and still the best place to do one. Leopards at a density found almost nowhere else, and a river full of hippos to fall asleep to.

name: Spitzkoppe & Sossusvlei
blurb: The oldest desert on earth, with red dunes over 300 metres high and a granite outcrop called the Matterhorn of Africa where San rock art dates back two thousand years.

name: Split
blurb: A living Roman palace with bars and flats built into its walls, and the best ferry connections to the Dalmatian islands.

name: St Kitts & Nevis
blurb: A UNESCO fortress guarding the old sugar trade on one island, and a quieter volcanic twin across a narrow strait where the beach sand is genuinely black.

name: St Moritz & the Engadin
