blurb: A high valley of lakes and larch at 1,800 metres, with 322 days of sun a year, the oldest winter resort in the world, and Romansh still spoken in the villages.

name: Stockholm
blurb: Fourteen islands of pastel waterfront and a 30,000-island archipelago beyond — long white summer nights, cosy candlelit winters.

name: Stonehenge & Avebury
blurb: Stones dragged 150 miles and raised five thousand years ago, aligned to midsummer sunrise by people who left no writing. Avebury up the road is bigger, older and you can walk among it.

name: Sucre & Potosí
blurb: A whitewashed colonial capital with the gentlest climate in Bolivia, and up the road the silver mountain that bankrolled the Spanish empire and swallowed eight million lives.

name: Sumba & West Timor
blurb: Savanna hills, megalithic villages with thatched towers, and a west-facing coast of empty barrels. Still one of the least-visited islands in Indonesia.

name: Svalbard
blurb: The northernmost town anyone lives in year-round, at 78°N — more polar bears than people, four months of unbroken darkness, and a law against dying there.

name: Svaneti
blurb: Medieval stone defence towers in villages under 5,000m Caucasus peaks — one of Europe's last genuinely remote mountain cultures.

name: Swedish Lapland
blurb: Abisko's famously clear 'blue hole' sky makes this one of the best aurora spots on earth — plus the Icehotel and Sámi reindeer country.

name: Sydney
blurb: The harbour, the Opera House and Bondi — a big city where people genuinely swim before work, with the Blue Mountains 90 minutes west.

name: Symi & the Dodecanese
blurb: A harbour of neoclassical mansions in ochre and terracotta stacked up both sides of a bay — built by sponge divers, abandoned, and now one of the prettiest arrivals in Greece.

name: Taipei
blurb: The best night-market food in Asia, hot springs on the metro line, and the friendliest big city in the region — and it's cheap.

name: Tallinn
blurb: A complete, intact medieval walled town wrapped around one of Europe's most digital societies — and still genuinely good value.

name: Tangier
blurb: Where Africa looks at Europe across fourteen miles of water. A century of spies, writers and smugglers has left a city that feels like it knows something you don't.

name: Taroko Gorge & Hualien
blurb: A marble canyon carved 1,000m deep, with tunnels and swing bridges cut into the cliffs, running down to a wild Pacific coast.

name: Tasmania
blurb: The cleanest air on earth, Cradle Mountain and the Overland Track, MONA's underground art museum, and convict history at Port Arthur.
photoTopics: Bay of Fires Tasmania orange rocks

name: Tayrona & Santa Marta
blurb: Jungle running straight into the Caribbean, with the Sierra Nevada rising to 5,700m behind it — snow and coral within forty miles of each other.

name: Tbilisi
blurb: Sulphur bathhouses, wooden balconies and Soviet brutalism stacked up a gorge — with 8,000 years of winemaking and Europe's best-value food scene.

name: Tel Aviv
blurb: Bauhaus architecture, 14km of city beach, one of the world's great LGBTQ+ scenes and a food culture punching far above its weight.
photoTopics: Bauhaus architecture Tel Aviv White City

name: Tenerife
blurb: Spain's highest mountain rising out of the Atlantic, black-sand beaches and reliably warm weather in the middle of a European winter.
photoTopics: Anaga rural park laurel forest Tenerife

name: Texel & the Wadden Islands
blurb: A chain of sandy islands along a tidal sea so productive it is a World Heritage Site, where the local sport is walking out across the mud at low tide to the next island.

name: The Aeolian Islands
blurb: Seven volcanic islands off Sicily, one of which has been erupting every twenty minutes for two thousand years and can be climbed at dusk to watch it.

name: The Åland Islands
blurb: Six thousand islands that belong to Finland, speak Swedish, fly their own flag and have been demilitarised since 1856. Bicycles and inter-island ferries are the transport.

name: The Alentejo
blurb: A third of Portugal, cork oaks and wheat to the horizon, marble towns, a Roman temple in Évora, and a wild Atlantic coast that the Algarve crowds never reach.

name: The Algarve
blurb: Golden cliffs, sea caves and hidden coves along Portugal's south coast, with excellent golf and some of Europe's best-value sun.

name: The Algerian Sahara
blurb: A sandstone plateau of rock arches and Neolithic art fifteen thousand years old, in a desert so empty the stars look artificial. Camel treks in, no roads at all.

name: The Andaman Islands
blurb: India's Thailand, 1,400km east of the mainland — Radhanagar's white sand, some of the cheapest diving certification anywhere, and almost nobody from outside India.

name: The Azores
blurb: Nine mid-Atlantic volcanic islands of crater lakes, hot springs and whale-watching — Europe's most convincing 'edge of the world'.

name: The Bahamas
blurb: Seven hundred islands of impossibly clear shallow water — swimming pigs at Exuma, blue holes, and the closest tropics to the US east coast.

name: The British Virgin Islands
blurb: The Caribbean's sailing capital — sixty islands close enough together to hop between under sail every day, with the Baths' giant granite boulders forming grottoes you swim through.

name: The Cape Verde Interior
blurb: Beyond the Sal beaches: Santo Antão's ribeiras dropping green and near-vertical to the sea, and Fogo, where people farm coffee inside a live volcano's caldera.

name: The Cayman Islands
blurb: Seven Mile Beach of powder-white sand, and offshore some of the clearest diving visibility in the Caribbean, with a sandbar where you can hand-feed stingrays standing waist-deep.

name: The Coffee Triangle
blurb: Steep green Andean valleys covered in coffee, with the Cocora Valley's 60-metre wax palms standing above the cloud like something that got the scale wrong.

name: The Costa Brava & Girona
blurb: Pine-backed coves between rocky headlands, a walled medieval city inland with a river of painted houses, and Dalí's museum an hour north in his home town.

name: The Cotswolds
blurb: Honey-coloured limestone villages in rolling hills, grown rich on wool six hundred years ago and preserved by having nothing much happen since.

name: The Curonian Spit
blurb: A ninety-eight-kilometre sand bar barely a few hundred metres wide, with dunes that swallowed fourteen villages, a lagoon on one side and the open Baltic on the other.

name: The Dead Sea
blurb: The lowest point on dry land, 430m below sea level, where the water is so saline you cannot sink. Mineral mud, spa resorts and biblical history.

name: The Dolomites
blurb: Pale limestone towers that turn pink at sunset, linked by the world's best ski circuit in winter and via ferrata in summer.

name: The Dordogne
blurb: Honey-stone villages on limestone cliffs above a slow river, foie gras and walnuts, and cave paintings at Lascaux made seventeen thousand years before any of it.

name: The Douro Valley
blurb: The oldest demarcated wine region in the world — terraces cut into schist so steep the vines are worked by hand, and a river you can go up by train, boat or road.

name: The Drakensberg
blurb: A 200km basalt escarpment with the world's second-highest waterfall down one side and 40,000 San rock paintings tucked into the caves along it.

name: The Everglades & Florida Keys
blurb: A river of grass sixty miles wide, alligators and manatees in the same water, and a highway running 113 miles across bridges to a bar in Key West at the end of it.

name: The Flinders Ranges
blurb: Ancient folded mountains older than complex life on earth, a natural amphitheatre of peaks called Wilpena Pound, and fossils from half a billion years before dinosaurs.

name: The Great Lakes & Mackinac Island
blurb: A freshwater island where cars have been banned since 1898 — fudge shops, horse-drawn carriages, and Lake Michigan's dune-backed coast a ferry ride away.

name: The Great Ocean Road
blurb: 243km of road built by returning soldiers, running past limestone stacks, rainforest gullies full of koalas, and surf beaches that face straight into the Southern Ocean.

name: The Great Smoky Mountains
blurb: The most visited national park in America and still enormous enough to lose yourself in — 800 miles of trail, 1,500 bears, and the blue haze the Cherokee named it for.

name: The High Tatras
blurb: The smallest alpine range in the world, packing 2,600m granite peaks, tarns and chamois into an area you can cross on foot in two days. Skiing in winter, huts in summer.

name: The Hunza Valley
blurb: Where three of the world's great mountain ranges collide — the Karakoram, Himalaya and Hindu Kush all visible from one valley, terraced with apricot orchards and famous for its long-lived elders.

name: The Isle of Man
blurb: A self-governing island with the oldest continuous parliament on earth, a steam railway, tail-less cats, and for two weeks each year the most dangerous motorcycle race there is.
photoTopics: Isle of Man TT motorcycle race
Isle of Man dark sky stars

name: The Jurassic Coast
blurb: Ninety-five miles of cliff recording 185 million years of geology, with Durdle Door, a fossil beach where Mary Anning changed palaeontology, and unexpectedly good swimming.

name: The Kalahari & Makgadikgadi
blurb: Salt pans the size of Switzerland, so flat and empty that you can see the curve of the earth. Meerkats that will stand on your head, and one of the last places with genuine silence.

name: The Loire Valley
blurb: Three hundred châteaux along one river, built when French kings had more money than sense — Chambord has 440 rooms and a double-helix staircase possibly designed by Leonardo.

name: The Maldives
blurb: Twenty-six atolls of overwater villas and house reefs. The single most reliable place on earth for a honeymoon — at a price.

name: The Masurian Lakes
blurb: Two thousand lakes joined by canals in Poland's north-east, sailed rather than driven, with Teutonic castles on the shores and the Wolf's Lair rotting in the forest.

name: The Middle Atlas & Ifrane
blurb: Cedar forests full of Barbary macaques, alpine-looking towns with red-tiled roofs, and snow in winter — the Morocco that surprises people who came for the desert.

name: The Omo Valley
blurb: Home to some of the last traditional tribal cultures on earth, largely unchanged for centuries — the Mursi, Hamer and Karo peoples still practise lip plates and bull-jumping ceremonies.

name: The Outer Banks
blurb: A hundred miles of barrier islands where the Wright brothers first flew, wild ponies still roam a beach with no road, and lighthouses mark a coast known for wrecking ships.

name: The Outer Hebrides
blurb: A hundred-mile chain of islands off the Atlantic edge — white shell beaches over turquoise water, standing stones older than Stonehenge, and Gaelic still the everyday language.

name: The Pantanal & Bonito
blurb: The world's largest wetland, and by some distance the best place on earth to see a jaguar. Down the road, rivers so clear you snorkel them like an aquarium.

name: The Paraguayan Chaco
blurb: A vast dry thornforest twice the size of England, home to Mennonite farming colonies, jaguars, and roads so straight and empty they disappear into heat shimmer.

name: The Peak District
blurb: Britain's first national park and still its busiest — gritstone edges for climbers, limestone dales for walkers, and Chatsworth if the weather turns, which it will.

name: The Peloponnese
blurb: Ancient Olympia, Mycenae, Epidaurus and Sparta on one peninsula, plus the Mani's stone tower villages and Nafplio, which is the prettiest town in Greece.

name: The Simien Mountains
blurb: Escarpments dropping 1,500 metres in one go, troops of gelada monkeys grazing on the edge, and thin cold air at 4,000 metres. Trek it; there is no other way to see it.

name: The Solomon Islands
blurb: Nearly a thousand islands, WWII wrecks encrusted with coral you can dive straight from the beach, and traditional custom villages where life runs much as it did a century ago.

name: The Sporades
blurb: Pine forest running down to sand, the clearest water in the Aegean, and a marine park protecting the last few hundred Mediterranean monk seals.

name: The Sundarbans
blurb: The largest mangrove forest on earth, a maze of tidal channels shared between Bangladesh and India, and the only place where Bengal tigers regularly swim between islands.

name: The Tunisian Sahara
blurb: The gateway to the Sahara, with a hot spring bubbling straight out of the dunes and Star Wars sets left standing in the desert since 1976, slowly filling with sand again.

name: The Usambara Mountains
blurb: A cool, misty highland forest older than the Himalayas, with more endemic species than almost anywhere on earth and hiking between villages instead of lodges.

name: The Westfjords
blurb: The part of Iceland the ring road misses — a shredded peninsula of table mountains and hot pools, Europe's largest bird cliff, and roads that close all winter.

name: Thessaloniki
blurb: Greece's second city and its best for eating — Byzantine walls, Ottoman baths, a huge student population, and a waterfront promenade built for the evening stroll.

name: Ticino & Lugano
blurb: Switzerland with palm trees and Italian menus — lakes Lugano and Maggiore under steep green mountains, grotti serving polenta, and the Verzasca's water impossibly clear.

name: Tikal & the Petén
blurb: Maya temples pushing up through rainforest canopy, with howler monkeys at dawn and toucans overhead. Climb Temple IV at sunrise and there is nothing above the trees but pyramids.

name: Tobago
blurb: Trinidad's sleepy sibling — the oldest protected rainforest in the western hemisphere, coral reefs a few strokes from the beach, and almost none of the crowds its neighbour draws for Carnival.
photoTopics: Buccoo Reef Tobago glass bottom boat

name: Tofino & Vancouver Island
blurb: A surf town at the edge of the temperate rainforest, storm-watching in winter, whale watching in summer, and old-growth cedars a few minutes from the beach.

name: Tokyo
blurb: The most rewarding city on earth to simply wander: more Michelin stars than anywhere, immaculate transport, and a different world down every side street.

name: Toledo & Segovia
blurb: Two fortress towns an hour from Madrid: Toledo in a river gorge, where Christians, Muslims and Jews built side by side, and Segovia under a Roman aqueduct with no mortar in it.

name: Tonga
blurb: The only Pacific nation never colonised, and one of very few places on earth where you may legally swim with humpback whales and their calves.

name: Toronto
blurb: Arguably the most multicultural city on earth — half its residents were born abroad, and you can eat your way around the world in one neighbourhood.

name: Torres del Paine
blurb: Three granite towers over a turquoise lake, with the W and O circuits beneath them — arguably the finest trekking park on the planet. Ferocious wind.

name: Toruń & Białowieża
blurb: A Gothic brick town the war somehow missed, where Copernicus was born and gingerbread has been baked to the same recipe since the 1300s — with Europe's last primeval forest east of it.

name: Transylvania & Brașov
blurb: Saxon fortified churches, painted medieval towns under the Carpathians, and Europe's largest population of brown bears living genuinely wild in the forest above them.

name: Trieste
blurb: Italy's least Italian city — a Habsburg seaport of grand cafés where Joyce wrote Ulysses, wedged between the Adriatic and a limestone plateau full of caves.

name: Trinidad
blurb: The birthplace of Carnival, calypso and the steelpan, an island that is more industrial than idyllic and considerably more interesting for it — plus leatherback turtles nesting on the north coast.

name: Tromsø
blurb: The Arctic's most liveable small city and Europe's most reliable aurora base — dog-sledding, whale-watching and a surprising bar scene.

name: Tulum & the Riviera Maya
blurb: Maya ruins on a cliff above a Caribbean beach, cenotes in the jungle behind, and the world's second-largest barrier reef offshore.

name: Tunisia
blurb: Carthage and the vast Roman amphitheatre at El Djem, blue-and-white Sidi Bou Said, and the Sahara sets where Star Wars was filmed.
photoTopics: Sidi Bou Said blue white Tunisia

name: Turin & the Langhe
blurb: A baroque city of arcaded boulevards and historic cafés under the Alps, with Barolo country an hour south and white truffles in the autumn markets.

name: Turks & Caicos
blurb: Grace Bay is regularly voted the best beach in the world — twelve miles of powder-soft sand and a reef a short swim out. Very quiet, very expensive.
photoTopics: Grace Bay Beach Turks and Caicos

name: Turku & the Archipelago
blurb: Finland's oldest city, with a medieval castle and a river of moored restaurant ships, opening into an archipelago of forty thousand islands you can cycle round on ferries.

name: Tyrol & Innsbruck
blurb: A city with a ski jump in it and mountains on all four sides — two Winter Olympics, and lift access straight from the old town.

name: Udaipur
blurb: White palaces floating on Lake Pichola beneath the Aravalli hills — India's most romantic city, and a calm counterpoint to the rest of Rajasthan.

name: Uluru & the Red Centre
blurb: A 348m sandstone monolith that changes colour through the day, sacred to the Anangu for tens of thousands of years, under the clearest skies in Australia.

name: Uruguay Coast
blurb: Montevideo's easy pace, José Ignacio's low-key glamour and Punta del Este's high season — plus the most progressive society in Latin America.
photoTopics: Punta del Este La Mano sculpture

name: Ushuaia & Tierra del Fuego
blurb: The southernmost city there is, on the Beagle Channel with the Andes falling into it. Where Antarctic ships leave from, and where the road simply stops.
photoTopics: End of the world sign Ushuaia

name: Utah's Mighty Five & Moab
blurb: Arches, Canyonlands, Zion, Bryce and Capitol Reef on one road trip — red rock, slot canyons and some of the darkest skies in America.
photoTopics: Utah red rock night sky Milky Way

name: Valencia
blurb: Spain's most liveable big city: paella's birthplace, a park where the river used to be, and a proper beach on the tram line.
photoTopics: City of Arts and Sciences Valencia

name: Valparaíso
blurb: Forty-two hills of corrugated-iron houses painted every colour there is, joined by Victorian funiculars, with the best street art in the hemisphere on every wall.

name: Vancouver
blurb: Mountains, ocean and old-growth forest all inside the city — you can ski and sail on the same day. It rains for half the year.
photoTopics: Sea to Sky Highway British Columbia

name: Vanuatu
blurb: Eighty islands where you can stand on the rim of an active volcano at night and watch it throw lava, then swim in a blue hole so clear it looks retouched.

name: Varanasi
blurb: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities on earth, where life and death happen openly on the Ganges ghats. Confronting and unforgettable.

name: Varna & the Black Sea Coast
blurb: Bulgaria's 'maritime capital' — Roman baths and a leafy seafront Sea Garden in the city itself, with the package-holiday beaches of Golden Sands and Sunny Beach a short ride up the coast.

name: Venice
blurb: There is nowhere else like it, and everyone knows — which is the problem. Astonishing in February fog, overwhelming in July.

name: Vermont & the Fall Foliage
blurb: Covered bridges, maple syrup and white church spires, at their absolute best for two weeks in October when the whole state turns red and gold.

name: Verona & Lake Garda
blurb: A Roman arena still used for opera every summer, a river bend full of pink marble, and Italy's biggest lake half an hour north with Alps at the far end of it.

name: Victoria Falls
blurb: The largest sheet of falling water on earth, throwing spray 400m into the air — plus white-water rafting on the Zambezi below it.

name: Vienna
blurb: Imperial palaces, the world's great concert halls and coffee houses you can occupy for hours — repeatedly voted the most liveable city on earth.

name: Vientiane & the Plain of Jars
blurb: The sleepiest capital in Southeast Asia, French colonial villas beside golden stupas, and up-country a plateau scattered with thousands of stone jars nobody can fully explain.

name: Vieques & Culebra
blurb: Two small islands off Puerto Rico with wild horses on the roads, Flamenco Beach on every list of the world's best, and the brightest bioluminescent bay on earth.

name: Vilnius
blurb: One of Europe's largest baroque old towns, a self-declared artists' republic across the river, and almost no crowds.

name: Vis & Korčula
blurb: Vis was closed to foreigners as a military base until 1989 and is still the least spoiled Adriatic island. Korčula claims Marco Polo and makes very good white wine.

name: Warsaw
blurb: Rebuilt from rubble and now unmistakably confident — a meticulously reconstructed old town beside glass towers and a serious food scene.
photoTopics: Palace of Culture and Science Warsaw

name: Washington DC
blurb: Nineteen Smithsonian museums, all free, plus the monuments and the cherry blossoms in early April. The best-value cultural city in America.

name: Wellington
blurb: The world's windiest capital, wedged between a harbour and steep hills, with more cafés per head than New York and the country's best museum for free.

name: Whistler
blurb: North America's largest ski area across two mountains joined by a record-breaking gondola — and the continent's best bike park in summer.

name: Whitsunday Islands
blurb: Seventy-four islands in the reef, and Whitehaven Beach — seven kilometres of silica sand so pure it squeaks. Best seen from a bareboat charter.

name: Wrocław
blurb: A city on twelve islands with more bridges than Venice, a market square rebuilt from rubble, and around three hundred small bronze dwarfs hidden at ankle height.

name: Yala & Udawalawe
blurb: The highest density of leopards anywhere, plus wild elephants in herds — Asia's most accessible and affordable safari.

name: Yangon
blurb: The largest surviving colonial townscape in Southeast Asia, mouldering gently under the gold of the Shwedagon — a stupa that has been rebuilt and regilded for a thousand years.

name: Yellowstone & Grand Teton
blurb: A supervolcano's worth of geysers and hot springs, bison herds and wolves, with the Tetons rising straight off the valley floor to the south.

name: Yerevan & Armenia
blurb: A pink tuff city looking straight at Mount Ararat across a closed border, with fourth-century monasteries on cliff edges an hour in any direction and a serious brandy habit.

name: Yogyakarta
blurb: Java's cultural heart — a working sultan's palace, batik and gamelan, and the colossal temples of Borobudur and Prambanan on the doorstep.

name: York
blurb: Two thousand years of city inside a complete set of medieval walls — Roman fortress, Viking capital, and a cathedral with the largest expanse of medieval stained glass in the world.

name: Yosemite
blurb: Granite walls a kilometre high, giant sequoias and waterfalls at full roar in May. The birthplace of big-wall climbing, and of the national park idea.

name: Yunnan & Lijiang
blurb: An old Naxi trading town of canals and cobbles below the Jade Dragon Snow Mountain, gateway to Tiger Leaping Gorge, one of the deepest and most dramatic canyons walked anywhere.

name: Zadar
blurb: A Roman forum, a sea organ that plays the waves through pipes under the promenade, and what Hitchcock called the most beautiful sunset in the world. Also, no cruise ships.

name: Zagreb
blurb: An Austro-Hungarian capital that most people fly straight past — café culture on a par with Vienna at a third of the price, and the world's only Museum of Broken Relationships.
photoTopics: Zagreb upper town St Marks church

name: Zakopane & the Polish Tatras
blurb: Poland's winter capital, all carved timber and smoked sheep's cheese, with the Tatras rising straight behind it and a funicular up Gubałówka for the view back.

name: Zanzibar
blurb: Stone Town's Swahili-Omani labyrinth of carved doors and spice markets, with turquoise sandbank beaches and dhows on the north coast.

name: Zermatt
blurb: Car-free, under the Matterhorn, with skiing possible 365 days a year on the glacier. Superb, and priced for people who know it.

name: Zurich
blurb: A banking city that swims in its own river, with excellent galleries, a serious club scene and the highest prices in Europe.
